reviewer: independent-reviewer-1, did not build; six throwaway /tmp clones; item branch never checked out in the real repo, nothing pushed, main never touched, no git internals
disposition: The safety half is real and it is the half attacked hardest. 23 laundering routes driven end to end through the shipped dispatcher and NONE produced a green: no route reached exit 0 under a selector, none emitted the aggregate line the gate reads, and .warp/last_verify was byte-identical AND mtime_ns-identical after every one. Naming every fragment (comma form, repeated flags, and --upto the last fragment) RUNS ALL 14 and still exits 2 with no aggregate line, so partiality is decided by the SELECTOR, not by how much ran. Label identity re-measured independently per fragment in both directions: 14 of 14 identical in order, 0 missing, 0 extra, 0 outcome deltas. Nothing found rises to wrong behaviour.

criteria.note: Re-measured, not read. The reviewer's own harness wrapped shared.expect and tagged every label with its emitting fragment: all 14 fragments reproduce their own label list IDENTICAL AND IN ORDER under shared+closure, 0 missing / 0 extra / 0 outcome deltas / 0 crashes, and each closure run's actual run list equalled requires.json. THE FIXPOINT IS LOAD-BEARING AND WAS REPRODUCED: direct demand only gives 8 of 13 CLOSED and 5 of 13 producing ZERO of their own labels (04, 08, 09, 10 on NameError 'ME'; 13 on NameError '_FakeLoop'). transitive_close(direct_demand(...)) == the committed requires.json, and 5 fragments GROW under the closing step. Regeneration is a byte no-op and wired into check_generated.sh. NOT --upto renamed: closure is a STRICT subset of the prefix for 11 of 13 and EQUALS it for 2 (01, 02). Timings within ~2%: --suite 05 0.08s vs --upto 05 21.82s; --suite 12 60.02s vs --upto 12 75.17s; union 05,09 == 09 alone. NO CARDINALITY PIN: appending TWO fragments left the suite green at 3389.

23 ROUTES DRIVEN, ZERO LAUNDERED. In every selector run: exit 2 (never 0), the anchored ^selftest: N passed, M failed$ matched NOTHING, the banner named the run PARTIAL, and .warp/last_verify was unchanged by sha256 AND mtime_ns. Sharpest: --suite <all 14> and --upto <last> each RUN ALL 14 and report 3387 passed, yet emit 'selftest (PARTIAL, 14 of 14 suites)' and exit 2. THE GATE PATH IS INDEPENDENTLY CLOSED: verify.sh byte-identical at both commits (sha256 807e7f5b663e1bae, the recorded digest), its only unit slot carries no selector, and it is read by indirect expansion so an EXPORTED CHECK_unit cannot reach it. SEVEN guard mutations re-driven with substitution count asserted ==1 and sha256 asserted changed then restored: 7 RED, 0 GREEN, 0 CRASH, 0 NOT_APPLIED, baseline GREEN - including M11b, the exact banner shape that used to CRASH.

The amendment is TRUE, not a dodge, checked three ways: .warp/packs.json declares 7 roots, none holds scripts/selftest.py; and `git log --all --diff-filter=A` over plugin/templates/scripts/selftest.py and packs/*/scripts/selftest.py returns NOTHING, so no selftest.py has EVER existed there in history. Engine canon byte-unchanged (git diff over plugin, packs, .warp is EMPTY). Landing condition re-derived from scratch at both commits and compared PER FRAGMENT IN ORDER: every one of the 13 pre-existing fragments identical, 0 moved, 0 lost, the entire +25 in fragment 14. VERDICT CLEAN. RULE #1 clean across 15 files and 3 commit messages.

claim_corrections: C1 THE MOST IMPORTANT. proof/WARP-0717/manifest.json and commit f1aa4c9 both say failing-witnesses.json records 'its substitution count and the sha256 before, after and restored'. THE ARTIFACT DOES NOT RECORD THEM - every witness carries exactly four keys (mutation, verdict, failed_assertions, detail). So the battery's STRONGEST property, that a mutation which failed to apply is reported NOT_APPLIED rather than as a guard that held, is UNAUDITABLE FROM THE RECORD. Either add the fields and regenerate, or delete the two sentences. Compensated by re-driving 7 of 14 with the reviewer's own applied-and-restored assertions, all 7 RED, so it is a RECORD defect not a guard defect.

C2 limits item 4 says 'a fragment edited to depend on something outside its closure will fail under --suite and pass under the full run'. MEASURED FALSE IN THE UNSAFE DIRECTION: it can also PASS VACUOUSLY under --suite with the SAME LABEL AND OUTCOME. Driven with a planter fragment setting an attribute on a module (a MUTATED OBJECT, so no NameError) and a reader iterating it: --suite <reader> exited 2 with 0 failures, the assertion iterating an EMPTY list and passing, while the full run iterated 2 real rows and also passed. Label identity held while the subset proved strictly nothing. Honest sentence: 'will fail under --suite, OR pass for a weaker reason with the same label'.

C3 THE EQUALS FORM BYPASSES THE REFUSAL. _flag_values does not recognise `--suite=<name>`, so BOTH `--suite=05_...` and `--suite=no_such_suite` fall through to a FULL run, exit 0, printing 'selftest: 3387 passed, 0 failed'. It fails in the SAFE direction (a genuine full run happened, so the line is true and nothing was laundered), hence not blocking - but the refusal is incomplete and someone chasing a fast loop silently pays the whole suite. FIX: refuse any unrecognised argument starting with '--', which also closes the equals form for --upto.

C4 docs/runbook.md presents three guards as equally live when only the aggregate line and the exit code have production callers today. The module, spec and manifest all disclose this; the operator text does not. Overstates in the SAFE direction. Add one clause naming the non-zero exit status as today's mechanism.

C5 'THE CLOSURE TABLE IS DERIVED, NOT TYPED' is only half true GOING FORWARD, and the untrue half governs every fragment added from now on: post-cut fragments have no region range, so direct_demand takes the HAND-TYPED `requires` in manifest.json at face value and merely closes it transitively. MEASURED CONSEQUENCE: a fragment declaring `requires: [itself]` while using a name another fragment binds was ACCEPTED by the generator, check_generated.sh PASSED, and `--suite <it>` died with a NameError traceback, exit 1, AND NO VERDICT LINE AT ALL - the dead-run shape this repo calls worse than a red. Fail-closed covers a MISSING declaration, never a WRONG one.

C6 the proof manifest binds itself to 00b0e22, one commit BEHIND the item's HEAD f1aa4c9, which is the commit carrying the evidence it cites. PROOF_REQ requires the key to be present, not to equal HEAD. Restamp it.

C7 the per-fragment 'against the prefix' numbers in the AC1 amendment and inner-loop-measurement.json are MODELLED, not measured (prefix_modelled_s / closure_modelled_s beside a single closure_measured_s). Only timings.txt measured shipped commands. The reviewer's own runs land within ~2%, so substantively right - but say modelled where it is modelled.

C8 two assertions in fragment 14 use all() over an iterable with NO non-emptiness guard, so they would pass vacuously if it emptied: the hostile-selector results are keyed BY THE BAD NAME with no len() binding, and the canon-absence assertion is vacuously true over an empty pack roster. Both fire correctly today. Bind each all() to the length of its own literal source.
cross_item_findings: X1 THE TRAILING-SLASH FOOTPRINT DEFECT REACHES FOUR OTHER SHIPPED SPECS. `.warp/arch._glob_re` gives a trailing slash no meaning, so `scripts/suites/` compiles to ^scripts/suites/$ and matches NO file path, while `scripts/suites/**` compiles correctly. Measured by driving shape_gate.footprint_findings over a representative diff each: WARP-0712 declares three such entries and produces 3 findings; WARP-0718, WARP-0719 and WARP-0720 each declare `docs/` and produce 1 each. The footprint rule is BLOCKING, `docs/` is NOT diff-excluded (only proof/ is), and WARP-1102 wired enforcement 2026-07-22 BEFORE 0712 landed. So FOUR SHIPPED SPECS CARRY FOOTPRINT DECLARATIONS THAT ASSERT NOTHING. WARP-0717 at HEAD produces 0. Needs its own item: convert every trailing-slash entry to the `path/**` form AND add a gate check refusing a footprint glob that matches no path in the tree, since a declaration that can never match is exactly the vacuous check this corpus forbids.

X2 scripts/suite_extract.py STILL EMBEDS THE PRE-0717 DISPATCHER AS A TEMPLATE. Its DISPATCHER string is the old selftest.py with no RunScope, no --suite and no banner, and its SHARED_PRELUDE holds the old UNCONDITIONAL report(). scripts/selftest.py is NOT in check_generated.sh, so nothing holds them in step. RE-RUNNING THAT MIGRATION TOOL WOULD SILENTLY REVERT AC2'S ENTIRE MECHANISM while leaving the fragments intact. Delete the stale templates or head them with a comment naming WARP-0717 as historical.

rulings_on_the_admissions.forward_guards: HONEST, if anything conservative. verify_stamp_payload and unit_evidence_check appear ONLY in run_scope.py's own definition/docstring and fragment 14's assertions - zero production callers, exactly as declared. aggregate_line has one caller, exit_code two. Today's mechanism is the exit status and the reviewer drove that chain end to end: verify.sh stamps green only on success, the slot carries no selector, an exported CHECK_unit cannot override the in-file assignment, and all 23 routes returned 2 or 1, never 0. The guards are labelled as forward guards in the module, spec, manifest AND assertion text. That is the difference between a real guard and a decorative one, and the item is on the right side of it.
rulings_on_the_admissions.kind_not_status: HONEST and UNDERSTATED. Driven against the real check_required_evidence: no checks entry is REFUSED; {unit, passed} accepted; {unit, FAILED} ACCEPTED; {unit, status 'lolno'} ACCEPTED; {unit} with NO status key ACCEPTED. It computes evidence_kinds_in_proof and tests only `accepted & present`, never reading a status. So the builder's rewritten assertion is exactly right and the earlier draft claiming a flipped status was rejected was correctly measured FALSE and deleted. The refusal buys WITHHOLDING the record, never rejecting a forged one. Does NOT undercut AC2: AC2 was amended to say exactly this, and the load-bearing sentence rests on the exit code.
